41: - **Correctness**: Output matches hand-calculated reference values

54: | CAPM | Rf=6%, β=1.2, Rm=15% | 16.8% | CAPM |

# 💰 Personal Finance MCP

> Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.

<!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
[![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)

**Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
**Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`

## Demo

[![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)

▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.

> **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
> may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
> (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).

---

## Overview

Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
single prioritised plan.

It runs three ways from one codebase:

- **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
- **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
- **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.

### Highlights

- 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
- 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
- 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
- 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
- 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.

---

## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories

| Category | Tools | Examples |
|----------|:----:|----------|
| Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
| Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
| Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
| Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
| Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
| Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
| Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
| Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
| Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
| Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
| Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
| Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
| Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |

Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).

"""
Personal Finance MCP Server

A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.

Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
"""

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
from .tools import (
    tvm,
    debt,
    planning,
    bonds,
    stocks,
    mutual_funds,
    portfolio,

    india_savings,
    cashflow,
    risk_profile,
    advisor,
    marketdata,
)

# Initialize the MCP server
mcp = FastMCP(
    "Personal Finance Advisor",
    instructions=(
        "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
        "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
        "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
        "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
        "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
        "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
        "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
        "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
        "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
        "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
        "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
        "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
        "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
        "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
        "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
        "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
        "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
        "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
        "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
        "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
        "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
        "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
        "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
        "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
        "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
        "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
        "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
        "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
        "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
        "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
        "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
    ),
    # Public HTTP connector: allow any host/origin (e.g. the Hugging Face Space
    # domain) and run stateless so it works behind a proxy / multiple workers.
    stateless_http=True,
    transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(
        enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False,
        allowed_hosts=["*"],
        allowed_origins=["*"],
    ),
)

# Register all tool modules

tvm.register(mcp)
debt.register(mcp)
planning.register(mcp)
bonds.register(mcp)
stocks.register(mcp)
mutual_funds.register(mcp)
portfolio.register(mcp)
derivatives.register(mcp)
india_savings.register(mcp)
cashflow.register(mcp)
risk_profile.register(mcp)
advisor.register(mcp)
marketdata.register(mcp)

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. Drop or fix every rejected requirement. It writes nothing.

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

---

# Quality Strategy & Test Plan Skill

This skill builds a quality strategy and test plan from a list of project requirements.

## Steps

1. **Receive requirements** — Accept the input as a block of text. Assume each line or numbered item is a requirement unless marked out-of-scope.
2. **Extract scope and out-of-scope** — Identify requirements explicitly labeled "out-of-scope" or "Out of scope". The rest are in scope.
3. **Identify risks** — For each in-scope requirement, list one or more risks (what could go wrong). Use the [risk-ranking-guide](references/risk-ranking-guide.md) to assign likelihood (Low/Medium/High) and impact (Low/Medium/High).
4. **Define test levels** — Describe what each level covers, using the [test-levels-guide](references/test-levels-guide.md).
   - Unit tests
   - Integration tests
   - End-to-end tests
5. **Specify entry and exit criteria** — Decide overall conditions for starting and ending testing.
6. **List test environments and data** — Describe what environments and test data are needed.
7. **Build traceability table** — Map each requirement to the tests that verify it, using the [traceability-table template](assets/traceability-table.csv).
8. **Assemble document** — Write the final document following the [quality-strategy-output template](assets/quality-strategy-output.md).

## Files

- `references/quality-strategy-template.md` — Template for the full document structure.
- `references/risk-ranking-guide.md` — Guidance on ranking risks.
- `references/test-levels-guide.md` — Descriptions of test levels.
- `assets/quality-strategy-output.md` — Final document output template.
- `assets/traceability-table.csv` — Traceability table CSV template.

## Constraints

- Only use information from the input. Do not add external details.
- Risks must be plausible and derived from the requirements.
- The document must include all sections from the template.

Personal Finance MCP Server

A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.

Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
"""

)

    "Personal Finance Advisor",
    instructions=(
        "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "

        "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
        "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
        "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
        "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
        "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
        "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
        "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
        "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
        "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
        "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
        "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
        "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
        "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
        "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
        "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
        "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
        "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
        "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
        "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
        "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
        "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
        "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
        "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
        "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
        "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
        "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
        "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
        "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
    ),

    stateless_http=True,
    transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(
        enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False,
        allowed_hosts=["*"],
        allowed_origins=["*"],
    ),
)

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

1: """
2: Personal Finance MCP Server
3: 
4: A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
5: for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.
6: 
7: Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
8: Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
9: """
10: 
11: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
12: from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
13: from .tools import (
14:     tvm,
15:     debt,
16:     planning,
17:     bonds,
18:     stocks,
19:     mutual_funds,
20:     portfolio,
21:     derivatives,
22:     india_savings,
23:     cashflow,
24:     risk_profile,
25:     advisor,
26:     marketdata,
27: )
28: 
29: # Initialize the MCP server
30: mcp = FastMCP(
31:     "Personal Finance Advisor",
32:     instructions=(
33:         "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
34:         "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
35:         "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
36:         "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
37:         "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
38:         "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
39:         "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
40:         "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
41:         "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
42:         "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
43:         "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
44:         "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
45:         "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
46:         "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
47:         "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
48:         "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
49:         "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
50:         "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
51:         "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
52:         "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
53:         "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
54:         "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
55:         "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
56:         "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
57:         "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
58:         "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
59:         "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
60:         "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
61:         "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
62:         "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
63:         "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
64:     ),
65:     # Public HTTP connector: allow any host/origin (e.g. the Hugging Face Space
66:     # domain) and run stateless so it works behind a proxy / multiple workers.
67:     stateless_http=True,
68:     transport_security=TransportSecuritySettings(
69:         enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False,
70:         allowed_hosts=["*"],
71:         allowed_origins=["*"],
72:     ),
73: )
74: 
75: # Register all tool modules
76: 
77: tvm.register(mcp)
78: debt.register(mcp)

6:   /api/* -> JSON endpoints for the website (tool catalog, calculators, live data)
7:   /           -> the exported Next.js website (static files)
8: 
9: Security: a transparent ASGI middleware adds security headers (incl. CSP) to every
10: response, caps request bodies, and rate-limits the JSON API. The calculator endpoint
11: validates and bounds all inputs (the calculators contain loops, so unbounded inputs
12: would be a denial-of-service vector).
13: 
14: Run:  python -m src.web         (PORT env var, defaults to 7860 for HF Spaces)
15: """

2: Production server runner for SSE transport.
3: 
4: Usage:
5:     python run_production.py
6:     python run_production.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000
7: 
8: Environment Variables:
9:     MCP_HOST  — Bind host (default: 127.0.0.1)
10:     MCP_PORT  — Bind port (default: 8000)
11: """
12: 
13: import os
14: import sys
15: 
16: 
17: def main():
18:     host = os.environ.get("MCP_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
19:     port = int(os.environ.get("MCP_PORT", "8000"))
20: 
21:     # Allow CLI overrides
22:     args = sys.argv[1:]
23:     i = 0
24:     while i < len(args):
25:         if args[i] == "--host" and i + 1 < len(args):
26:             host = args[i + 1]
27:             i += 2
28:         elif args[i] == "--port" and i + 1 < len(args):
29:             port = int(args[i + 1])
30:             i += 2
31:         else:
32:             i += 1
33: 
34:     from src.server import mcp
35: 
36:     print("Starting Personal Finance MCP Server (SSE)")
37:     print(f"  Host: {host}")
38:     print(f"  Port: {port}")
39:     print(f"  Tools: {len(mcp._tool_manager._tools)}")
40:     print(f"  URL:  http://{host}:{port}/sse")
41:     print()
42: 
43:     mcp.run(transport="sse", host=host, port=port)
44: 
45: 
46: if __name__ == "__main__":

1: # Testing Guide
2: 
3: ## Test Structure
4: 
5: ```
6: tests/
7: ├── test_tvm.py           # 16 tests — Time Value of Money
8: ├── test_debt.py          # 11 tests — Debt & Loan calculations
9: ├── test_ratios.py        #  9 tests — Financial ratios & health score
10: ├── test_bonds.py         # 10 tests — Bond pricing & yields
11: ├── test_stocks.py        #  8 tests — Stock valuation models
12: ├── test_mutual_funds.py  # 11 tests — MF/SIP calculations
13: ├── test_portfolio.py     # 19 tests — Portfolio analytics
14: ├── test_integration.py   # 18 tests — Server registration, output format, E2E scenarios
15: └── (total: 102 tests)
16: ```
17: 
18: ## Running Tests
19: 
20: ```bash
21: # Activate environment
22: source .venv/bin/activate
23: 
24: # Run all tests
25: pytest tests/ -v
26: 
27: # Run a specific module
28: pytest tests/test_tvm.py -v
29: 
30: # Run a specific test class
31: pytest tests/test_portfolio.py::TestSharpeRatio -v
32: 
33: # Run with coverage (install pytest-cov first)
34: pytest tests/ --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing
35: ```
36: 
37: ## Test Categories
38: 
39: ### Unit Tests (Calculator Layer)
40: Each calculator module has its own test file. Tests verify:
41: - **Correctness**: Output matches hand-calculated reference values
42: - **Edge cases**: Zero rates, negative values, boundary conditions
43: - **Error handling**: Invalid inputs (growth > return, zero denominators)
44: - **Consistency**: Inverse operations produce original values
45: 
46: ### Examples of Verified Calculations
47: 
48: | Test | Input | Expected | Method |
49: |------|-------|----------|--------|
50: | FV annual | PV=1L, r=10%, t=5y | ₹1,61,051 | Compound interest |
51: | FV monthly | PV=1L, r=12%, t=10y | ₹3,30,038.69 | Compound interest |
52: | EMI | P=50L, r=8.5%, t=20y | ₹43,391.16 | Amortized loan |
53: | Bond price | FV=1000, c=8%, YTM=10%, t=5y | ₹922.78 | DCF pricing |
54: | CAPM | Rf=6%, β=1.2, Rm=15% | 16.8% | CAPM |
55: | Sharpe | Rp=15%, Rf=6%, σ=8% | 1.125 | Sharpe ratio |
56: | DDM | D0=5, g=8%, r=15% | ₹77.14 | Gordon growth |
57: 
58: ## Adding New Tests
59: 
60: Follow the pattern:
61: 
62: ```python
63: from src.calculators.module_name import function_name
64: 
65: class TestFunctionName:
66:     def test_basic_case(self):
67:         result = function_name(inputs...)
68:         assert result["key"] == expected_value
69: 
70:     def test_edge_case(self):
71:         result = function_name(edge_inputs...)
72:         assert "error" in result or result["key"] satisfies condition
73: ```
74: 
75: ## Integration Testing
76: 
77: Test MCP tool layer (tools call calculators and format output):
78: 
79: ```python
80: # Quick integration test
81: python -c "
82: from src.server import mcp
83: import asyncio
84: 
85: async def test():
86:     tools = mcp._tool_manager._tools
87:     # Verify all tools are registered
88:     assert len(tools) == 54
89:     print('All 54 tools registered successfully')
90: 
91: asyncio.run(test())
92: "
93: ```

99:    - "Calculate EMI for a 50 lakh home loan at 8.5% for 20 years"
100:    - "What's my financial health score?" (provide details)
101:    - "Plan my retirement — I'm 30, earn 1.5L/month"
102:    - "Compare two bonds: 8% coupon vs 10% coupon, both 5 year"

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

"""
Time Value of Money Calculations

Core formulas:
  FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Future Value with compounding
  PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Present Value
  FV_continuous = PV × e^(r×t)         -- Continuous compounding
  FV_annuity = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1)/r]  -- Future Value of Annuity
  PV_annuity = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n)/r] -- Present Value of Annuity
  PV_perpetuity = PMT / r             -- Present Value of Perpetuity
  PV_growing_perpetuity = PMT / (r-g) -- Growing Perpetuity
  Rule of 72: Years to double ≈ 72 / rate
"""

import math


def future_value(
    pv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
) -> dict:
    """Calculate Future Value with compounding. FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
    r = annual_rate / 100
    n = compounding_periods
    t = years

    if n == 0:  # continuous compounding
        fv = pv * math.exp(r * t)
        formula = f"FV = PV × e^(r×t) = {pv:,.2f} × e^({r}×{t})"
    else:
        fv = pv * (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
        formula = f"FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {pv:,.2f} × (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"

    simple_interest = pv * r * t
    compound_benefit = fv - pv - simple_interest

    return {
        "future_value": round(fv, 2),
        "present_value": pv,
        "total_interest": round(fv - pv, 2),
        "simple_interest": round(simple_interest, 2),
        "compounding_benefit": round(compound_benefit, 2),
        "growth_multiple": round(fv / pv, 4),
        "formula": formula,
    }


def present_value(
    fv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
) -> dict:
    """Calculate Present Value. PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
    r = annual_rate / 100
    n = compounding_periods
    t = years

    if n == 0:  # continuous
        pv = fv * math.exp(-r * t)
        formula = f"PV = FV × e^(-r×t) = {fv:,.2f} × e^(-{r}×{t})"
    else:
        pv = fv / (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
        formula = f"PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {fv:,.2f} / (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"

    discount = fv - pv

    return {
        "present_value": round(pv, 2),
        "future_value": fv,
        "discount": round(discount, 2),
        "discount_factor": round(pv / fv, 6),
        "formula": formula,
    }

"""
Live Market Data (keyless public sources)

Wraps free, no-API-key endpoints so the MCP tools and the website dashboard share
one implementation:
  - Mutual-fund NAVs : api.mfapi.in (AMFI data)        -> get_mf_nav / search
  - FX rates         : api.frankfurter.app (ECB data)   -> get_fx_rate
  - Equity/index quote: stooq.com CSV                    -> get_quote

Network calls are best-effort and return {"error": ...} on failure so callers
never crash. These are the only non-deterministic tools in the server.
"""

import httpx

_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(8.0)
_UA = {"User-Agent": "personal-finance-mcp/1.1 (+https://github.com/sarveshtalele)"}


def search_mutual_funds(query: str, limit: int = 10) -> dict:
    """Search AMFI mutual-fund schemes by name; returns scheme codes + names."""
    try:
        r = httpx.get(
            "https://api.mfapi.in/mf/search",
            params={"q": query},

"""
Bond Pricing and Yield Calculations

Core formulas:
  Bond Price = Σ [C/(1+r)^t] + FV/(1+r)^n
  Current Yield = Annual Coupon / Market Price
  YTM: Price = Σ [C/(1+y)^t] + FV/(1+y)^n  (solved iteratively)
  Macaulay Duration = Σ [t × PV(CF_t)] / Bond Price
  Modified Duration = Macaulay Duration / (1 + y/n)
  Convexity = Σ [t(t+1) × PV(CF_t)] / (Price × (1+y)^2)
"""


def bond_price(
    face_value: float,
    coupon_rate: float,
    ytm: float,
    years_to_maturity: float,
    coupon_frequency: int = 2,
) -> dict:
    """
    Calculate bond price using DCF.
    Price = Σ [C/(1+r)^t] + FV/(1+r)^n
    """
    c = face_value * (coupon_rate / 100) / coupon_frequency
    r = ytm / 100 / coupon_frequency
    n = int(years_to_maturity * coupon_frequency)

    if r == 0:
        pv_coupons = c * n
        pv_face = face_value
    else:
        pv_coupons = c * (1 - (1 + r) ** (-n)) / r
        pv_face = face_value / (1 + r) ** n

    price = pv_coupons + pv_face

    if price > face_value:
        premium_discount = "Premium (Price > Face Value)"
    elif price < face_value:
        premium_discount = "Discount (Price < Face Value)"
    else:
        premium_discount = "At Par"

    return {
        "bond_price": round(price, 2),
        "pv_of_coupons": round(pv_coupons, 2),
        "pv_of_face_value": round(pv_face, 2),
        "coupon_per_period": round(c, 2),
        "total_periods": n,
        "premium_or_discount": premium_discount,
        "premium_discount_amount": round(price - face_value, 2),
        "formula": f"Price = Σ[{c:.2f}/(1+{r:.4f})^t] + {face_value}/(1+{r:.4f})^{n}",
    }


def current_yield(annual_coupon: float, market_price: float) -> dict:
    """Current Yield = Annual Coupon / Market Price"""
    cy = (annual_coupon / market_price) * 100

    return {
        "current_yield": round(cy, 4),
        "annual_coupon": annual_coupon,
        "market_price": market_price,
        "formula": f"CY = {annual_coupon} / {market_price} × 100 = {cy:.4f}%",
    }


def yield_to_maturity(
    face_value: float,
    coupon_rate: float,
    market_price: float,
    years_to_maturity: float,
    coupon_frequency: int = 2,
) -> dict:
    """
    Calculate YTM using iterative Newton-Raphson method.
    Solve: Price = Σ [C/(1+y)^t] + FV/(1+y)^n for y
    """
    c = face_value * (coupon_rate / 100) / coupon_frequency
    n = int(years_to_maturity * coupon_frequency)

    # Approximate YTM using formula:
    # YTM ≈ [C + (FV - P)/n] / [(FV + P)/2]
    annual_coupon = face_value * coupon_rate / 100
    approx_ytm = (annual_coupon + (face_value - market_price) / years_to_maturity) / (
        (face_value + market_price) / 2
    )

    # Newton-Raphson refinement
    ytm_guess = approx_ytm / coupon_frequency

    for _ in range(200):
        price = 0
        dprice = 0
        for t in range(1, n + 1):
            df = (1 + ytm_guess) ** t
            price += c / df
            dprice -= t * c / (df * (1 + ytm_guess))
        price += face_value / (1 + ytm_guess) ** n
        dprice -= n * face_value / ((1 + ytm_guess) ** n * (1 + ytm_guess))

        diff = price - market_price
        if abs(diff) < 0.0001:
            break
        ytm_guess -= diff / dprice

    ytm_annual = ytm_guess * coupon_frequency * 100

    return {
        "ytm": round(ytm_annual, 4),
        "ytm_per_period": round(ytm_guess * 100, 4),
        "approximate_ytm": round(approx_ytm * 100, 4),
        "market_price": market_price,
        "face_value": face_value,
        "coupon_rate": coupon_rate,
        "formula": "YTM ≈ [C + (FV - P)/n] / [(FV + P)/2]",
    }


def bond_duration(
    face_value: float,
    coupon_rate: float,
    ytm: float,
    years_to_maturity: float,
    coupon_frequency: int = 2,
) -> dict:

  Information Ratio: (R_p - R_b) / Tracking Error
  Sortino Ratio: (R_p - R_f) / Downside Deviation
"""

import math


def portfolio_expected_return(weights: list[float], returns: list[float]) -> dict:
    """E(Rp) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)"""
    if len(weights) != len(returns):

    portfolio_return = sum(w * r for w, r in zip(weights, returns))
    total_weight = sum(weights)

    contributions = [
        {"weight": round(w, 4), "return": r, "contribution": round(w * r, 4)}
        for w, r in zip(weights, returns)
    ]

    return {
        "portfolio_expected_return": round(portfolio_return, 4),
        "total_weight": round(total_weight, 4),
        "contributions": contributions,
        "formula": "E(Rp) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)",
    }


def portfolio_risk(
    weights: list[float],
    std_devs: list[float],
    correlations: list[list[float]],
) -> dict:
    """
    Portfolio variance and standard deviation.
    σ²p = ΣΣ w_i × w_j × σ_i × σ_j × ρ_ij
    """
    n = len(weights)
    if len(std_devs) != n or len(correlations) != n:
        return {"error": "Dimensions mismatch"}

    variance = 0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            variance += (
                weights[i] * weights[j] * std_devs[i] * std_devs[j] * correlations[i][j]

    std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)

    # Individual contributions
    risk_contributions = []
    for i in range(n):
        marginal = 0
        for j in range(n):
            marginal += weights[j] * std_devs[i] * std_devs[j] * correlations[i][j]
        marginal *= weights[i]
        risk_contributions.append(
            {
                "asset": i + 1,
                "weight": round(weights[i], 4),
                "individual_risk": round(std_devs[i], 4),

23:     Price = Σ [C/(1+r)^t] + FV/(1+r)^n
24:     """

26:     r = ytm / 100 / coupon_frequency

1: """
2: Portfolio Analytics and Modern Portfolio Theory
3: 
4: Core formulas:
5:   Expected Return: E(Rp) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)
6:   Portfolio Variance: σ²p = ΣΣ w_i × w_j × σ_i × σ_j × ρ_ij
7:   Beta: β = Cov(R_i, R_m) / Var(R_m)
8:   CAPM: E(R_i) = R_f + β × (E(R_m) - R_f)
9:   Sharpe Ratio: (R_p - R_f) / σ_p
10:   Treynor Ratio: (R_p - R_f) / β_p
11:   Jensen's Alpha: α = R_p - [R_f + β × (R_m - R_f)]
12:   Information Ratio: (R_p - R_b) / Tracking Error
13:   Sortino Ratio: (R_p - R_f) / Downside Deviation
14: """
15: 
16: import math
17: 
18: 
19: def portfolio_expected_return(weights: list[float], returns: list[float]) -> dict:
20:     """E(Rp) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)"""
21:     if len(weights) != len(returns):
22:         return {"error": "Weights and returns must have same length"}
23: 
24:     portfolio_return = sum(w * r for w, r in zip(weights, returns))
25:     total_weight = sum(weights)
26: 
27:     contributions = [
28:         {"weight": round(w, 4), "return": r, "contribution": round(w * r, 4)}
29:         for w, r in zip(weights, returns)
30:     ]
31: 
32:     return {
33:         "portfolio_expected_return": round(portfolio_return, 4),
34:         "total_weight": round(total_weight, 4),
35:         "contributions": contributions,
36:         "formula": "E(Rp) = Σ w_i × E(R_i)",
37:     }
38: 
39: 
40: def portfolio_risk(
41:     weights: list[float],
42:     std_devs: list[float],
43:     correlations: list[list[float]],
44: ) -> dict:
45:     """
46:     Portfolio variance and standard deviation.
47:     σ²p = ΣΣ w_i × w_j × σ_i × σ_j × ρ_ij
48:     """
49:     n = len(weights)
50:     if len(std_devs) != n or len(correlations) != n:
51:         return {"error": "Dimensions mismatch"}
52: 
53:     variance = 0
54:     for i in range(n):
55:         for j in range(n):
56:             variance += (

33:         "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
34:         "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
35:         "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
36:         "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
37:         "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
38:         "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
39:         "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
40:         "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
41:         "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
42:         "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
43:         "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
44:         "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
45:         "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
46:         "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
47:         "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
48:         "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
49:         "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
50:         "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.

3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.

2: Personal Finance MCP Server
3: 
4: A stateless MCP server providing deterministic personal finance calculations
5: for financial planning, investment analysis, and portfolio management.
6: 
7: Supports: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and any MCP-compatible client.
8: Transport: stdio (default), SSE (optional).
9: """

11: from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
12: from mcp.server.transport_security import TransportSecuritySettings
13: from .tools import (
14:     tvm,
15:     debt,
16:     planning,
17:     bonds,
18:     stocks,
19:     mutual_funds,
20:     portfolio,

22:     india_savings,
23:     cashflow,
24:     risk_profile,
25:     advisor,

30: mcp = FastMCP(
31:     "Personal Finance Advisor",
32:     instructions=(
33:         "Deterministic personal finance toolkit grounded in core financial-planning "
34:         "principles. Covers Time Value of Money, cash-flow & budgeting, debt "
35:         "management, Indian small-savings (PPF/SSY/NSC/KVP/SCSS/RD/FD/EPF), goal & "
36:         "retirement planning, stock/bond valuation, derivatives, mutual funds, portfolio "
37:         "analytics, risk profiling, and live market data (mutual-fund NAVs, FX, quotes).\n\n"
38:         "HOW TO ROUTE A USER STORY TO TOOLS:\n"
39:         "- The user will NOT name tools. Infer intent from their situation and pick tools "
40:         "by what they're trying to achieve.\n"
41:         "- When someone describes their finances broadly ('I'm 30, earn 1L/month, have a "
42:         "home loan, want to retire at 60'), START with `create_financial_plan` to get a "
43:         "prioritised action plan, then drill into specific calculators for detail.\n"
44:         "- Follow the planning order: evaluate position -> protect (emergency fund, "
45:         "insurance) -> reduce debt -> profile risk -> invest for goals.\n"
46:         "- Chain tools freely: e.g. assess_risk_profile -> suggest_asset_allocation -> "
47:         "calculate_sip_needed. Always show the numbers and the formula used.\n\n"
48:         "GOVERNANCE — STRICTLY FOLLOW (non-negotiable):\n"
49:         "1. Use ONLY numbers returned by these tools. Never invent, estimate, round "
50:         "differently, or substitute your own figures for a tool's output.\n"
51:         "2. Present allocations, percentages, EMIs, corpus and SIP amounts EXACTLY as "
52:         "the tool returned them. If you show a split, it must match the tool verbatim.\n"
53:         "3. Do NOT fabricate things the tools do not return: specific fund names or "
54:         "tickers, expected-return ranges, CAGR assumptions, tax rates, or multi-year "
55:         "projection tables. If the user wants a projection, call the relevant tool "
56:         "(e.g. plan_retirement, calculate_sip_returns) and report ITS numbers.\n"
57:         "4. There is ONE source of truth for an equity/debt/gold split: "
58:         "suggest_asset_allocation. assess_risk_profile returns the same split. If you "
59:         "have both, they will agree — never blend them or present a third number.\n"
60:         "5. If two tool results appear to conflict, do not silently pick one. Re-run "
61:         "with consistent inputs and surface the discrepancy to the user.\n"
62:         "6. Recompute via a tool whenever inputs change; never carry an earlier answer "
63:         "forward as if it still applies. State which tool produced each number."
64:     ),
65:     # Public HTTP connector: allow any host/origin (e.g. the Hugging Face Space
66:     # domain) and run stateless so it works behind a proxy / multiple workers.

72:     ),
73: )

1: """
2: Time Value of Money Calculations
3: 
4: Core formulas:
5:   FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Future Value with compounding
6:   PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Present Value
7:   FV_continuous = PV × e^(r×t)         -- Continuous compounding
8:   FV_annuity = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1)/r]  -- Future Value of Annuity
9:   PV_annuity = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n)/r] -- Present Value of Annuity
10:   PV_perpetuity = PMT / r             -- Present Value of Perpetuity
11:   PV_growing_perpetuity = PMT / (r-g) -- Growing Perpetuity
12:   Rule of 72: Years to double ≈ 72 / rate
13: """
14: 
15: import math
16: 
17: 
18: def future_value(
19:     pv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
20: ) -> dict:
21:     """Calculate Future Value with compounding. FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
22:     r = annual_rate / 100
23:     n = compounding_periods
24:     t = years
25: 
26:     if n == 0:  # continuous compounding
27:         fv = pv * math.exp(r * t)
28:         formula = f"FV = PV × e^(r×t) = {pv:,.2f} × e^({r}×{t})"
29:     else:
30:         fv = pv * (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
31:         formula = f"FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {pv:,.2f} × (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"
32: 
33:     simple_interest = pv * r * t
34:     compound_benefit = fv - pv - simple_interest
35: 
36:     return {
37:         "future_value": round(fv, 2),
38:         "present_value": pv,
39:         "total_interest": round(fv - pv, 2),
40:         "simple_interest": round(simple_interest, 2),
41:         "compounding_benefit": round(compound_benefit, 2),
42:         "growth_multiple": round(fv / pv, 4),
43:         "formula": formula,
44:     }

# Analyzing Repositories

Inspects a target repository codebase to produce a deterministic architecture manifest and stack profile.

## When to use
Activate this skill at the beginning of any test engineering engagement, or when the discover or start stage runs (plugin commands `qe-discover` and `qe-start`).

## Workflow
1. **Tree Scanning:** Enumerate all files, excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, and `.venv`.
2. **Manifest Parsing:** Read `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, `pom.xml`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`.
3. **Signal Detection:** Match tokens against [references/STACK_SIGNALS.md](references/STACK_SIGNALS.md).
4. **Test Inventory:** Identify existing test suites, file naming patterns (`*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`), and runner scripts.
5. **Output Generation:** Emit `01-discovery/architecture.json` in the target documentation folder.

## Mode detection
`--mode auto` detects; an explicit `greenfield` or `brownfield` wins.
- **Brownfield:** source files or tests exist. Record the existing test count as the regression baseline. Run nothing.
- **Greenfield:** no source code yet. Skip scanning. Record the intended stack from the user's stated stack, or ask. Next step is the stories stage.

## Platform code step
The platform runs the scan in code, not as a skill script. Given the repository directory, it returns JSON (languages, frameworks, test runners, manifests, source/test file counts, detected `mode`) and writes nothing. Implemented in `repos/scan.py`.

## Edge Cases
- **Monorepos:** Detect workspace roots (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, lerna, cargo workspaces) and shard analysis per package.
- **Minified Files:** Flag minified bundles and request unminified source code.

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. Drop or fix every rejected requirement. It writes nothing.

  <resource name="evals/evals.json"/>
  <resource name="references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md"/>
</available_resources>

name: read_skill_resource
content:
# Requirements Reverse-Engineering Rules

1. **Observable Behavior Rule:** Requirements must assert externally observable behavior (HTTP response codes, return values, emitted events, DOM changes). Never assert internal private variable state.
2. **Mandatory Source Quote Rule:** Every requirement must include:
   - `source_file`: relative path to real file.
   - `line_number`: 1-based start line.
   - `quote`: verbatim code snippet copied directly from source.
3. **Precedence Rule:** Executable code strictly takes precedence over comments. If a comment says "Always returns true" but code has an `if (...) return false;` branch, extract the real code behavior.
4. **Actors Rule:** Every requirement names exactly one actor or `system`.

# 💰 Personal Finance MCP

> Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.

<!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->

[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
[![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)

**Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
**Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`

## Demo

[![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)

▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.

> **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
> may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
> (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).

---

## Overview

Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
single prioritised plan.

It runs three ways from one codebase:

- **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
- **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
- **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.

### Highlights

- 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
- 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
- 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
- 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
- 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.

---

## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories

| Category | Tools | Examples |
|----------|:----:|----------|
| Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
| Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
| Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
| Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
| Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
| Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
| Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
| Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
| Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
| Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
| Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
| Risk Profiling | 1 | suitability score → suggested equity/debt split |
| Advisor | 1 | `create_financial_plan` — the story → plan orchestrator |

Browse them all (with live descriptions) at [`/tools`](https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/tools).

---

1: """
2: Time Value of Money Calculations
3: 
4: Core formulas:
5:   FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Future Value with compounding
6:   PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)           -- Present Value
7:   FV_continuous = PV × e^(r×t)         -- Continuous compounding
8:   FV_annuity = PMT × [((1+r)^n - 1)/r]  -- Future Value of Annuity
9:   PV_annuity = PMT × [(1 - (1+r)^-n)/r] -- Present Value of Annuity
10:   PV_perpetuity = PMT / r             -- Present Value of Perpetuity
11:   PV_growing_perpetuity = PMT / (r-g) -- Growing Perpetuity
12:   Rule of 72: Years to double ≈ 72 / rate
13: """
14: 
15: import math
16: 
17: 
18: def future_value(
19:     pv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
20: ) -> dict:
21:     """Calculate Future Value with compounding. FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
22:     r = annual_rate / 100
23:     n = compounding_periods
24:     t = years
25: 
26:     if n == 0:  # continuous compounding
27:         fv = pv * math.exp(r * t)
28:         formula = f"FV = PV × e^(r×t) = {pv:,.2f} × e^({r}×{t})"
29:     else:
30:         fv = pv * (1 + r / n) ** (n * t)
31:         formula = f"FV = PV × (1 + r/n)^(n×t) = {pv:,.2f} × (1 + {r}/{n})^({n}×{t})"
32: 
33:     simple_interest = pv * r * t
34:     compound_benefit = fv - pv - simple_interest
35: 
36:     return {
37:         "future_value": round(fv, 2),
38:         "present_value": pv,
39:         "total_interest": round(fv - pv, 2),
40:         "simple_interest": round(simple_interest, 2),
41:         "compounding_benefit": round(compound_benefit, 2),
42:         "growth_multiple": round(fv / pv, 4),
43:         "formula": formula,
44:     }
45: 
46: 
47: def present_value(
48:     fv: float, annual_rate: float, years: float, compounding_periods: int = 1
49: ) -> dict:
50:     """Calculate Present Value. PV = FV / (1 + r/n)^(n×t)"""
51:     r = annual_rate / 100
52:     n = compounding_periods
53:     t = years
54: 
55:     if n == 0:  # continuous
56:         pv = fv * math.exp(-r * t)
57:         formula = f"PV = FV × e^(-r×t) = {fv:,.2f} × e^(-{r}×{t})"

"""
Indian Small Savings & Deposit Instruments

Deterministic maturity calculators for the popular government/bank schemes
commonly used in Indian personal finance: PPF, Sukanya Samriddhi, NSC, KVP,
SCSS, Recurring Deposit, Fixed Deposit and EPF.

All rates are entered as annual percentages.
"""


def ppf_maturity(annual_deposit: float, annual_rate: float, years: int = 15) -> dict:
    """Public Provident Fund: yearly deposit, annual compounding, deposit at start of year."""
    r = annual_rate / 100
    balance = 0.0
    total_deposited = 0.0
    for _ in range(years):
        balance = (balance + annual_deposit) * (1 + r)
        total_deposited += annual_deposit
    return {
        "maturity_value": round(balance, 2),
        "total_deposited": round(total_deposited, 2),
        "total_interest": round(balance - total_deposited, 2),
        "years": years,
        "annual_rate": annual_rate,
        "formula": "Each year: balance = (balance + deposit) × (1 + r)",
    }


def sukanya_samriddhi(
    annual_deposit: float,
    annual_rate: float,
    deposit_years: int = 15,
    maturity_years: int = 21,
) -> dict:
    """Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana: deposits for 15 yrs, matures in 21 yrs, annual compounding."""
    r = annual_rate / 100
    balance = 0.0
    total_deposited = 0.0
    for year in range(1, maturity_years + 1):
        if year <= deposit_years:
            balance += annual_deposit
            total_deposited += annual_deposit
        balance *= 1 + r
    return {
        "maturity_value": round(balance, 2),
        "total_deposited": round(total_deposited, 2),
        "total_interest": round(balance - total_deposited, 2),
        "deposit_years": deposit_years,
        "maturity_years": maturity_years,
        "formula": "Deposit for 15 yrs, compound annually until year 21",
    }


def nsc_maturity(principal: float, annual_rate: float, years: int = 5) -> dict:
    """National Savings Certificate: lump sum, annual compounding, interest reinvested."""
    r = annual_rate / 100
    maturity = principal * (1 + r) ** years
    return {
        "maturity_value": round(maturity, 2),
        "principal": principal,
        "total_interest": round(maturity - principal, 2),
        "years": years,
        "formula": f"M = P × (1+r)^t = {principal:,.2f} × (1+{r})^{years}",
    }


def kvp_maturity(principal: float, annual_rate: float) -> dict:
    """Kisan Vikas Patra: doubles money; tenure derived from the prevailing rate."""
    import math

    r = annual_rate / 100
    years_to_double = math.log(2) / math.log(1 + r)
    return {
        "maturity_value": round(principal * 2, 2),
        "principal": principal,
        "years_to_double": round(years_to_double, 2),
        "months_to_double": round(years_to_double * 12),
        "annual_rate": annual_rate,
        "formula": "Solve (1+r)^t = 2  →  t = ln2 / ln(1+r)",
    }


def scss_payout(principal: float, annual_rate: float, years: int = 5) -> dict:
    """Senior Citizens Savings Scheme: quarterly interest payout, principal returned at maturity."""
    quarterly_interest = principal * (annual_rate / 100) / 4
    annual_income = quarterly_interest * 4
    return {
        "quarterly_payout": round(quarterly_interest, 2),
        "annual_income": round(annual_income, 2),
        "total_interest": round(annual_income * years, 2),
        "principal_returned": principal,
        "years": years,
        "formula": "Quarterly payout = Principal × rate / 4 (simple, paid out each quarter)",

name: extracting-requirements
description: Inverts codebases, public interfaces, and documentation into observable, testable requirements with verifiable evidence quotes. Use when extracting test requirements or preparing for test planning.
metadata:
  author: Sarvesh Talele
  version: "1.4.0"
---

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

## When to use
Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

## Workflow
0. **Mode:** Brownfield reads code. Greenfield reads the approved user stories file (`docs/qe/<app>/02-requirements/user_stories.md`) instead of code.
1. **Source Inspection:** Locate route handlers, controllers, CLI command parsers, and business rules.
2. **Behavior Identification:** Express requirements in observable terms ("System returns 403 when token is expired").
3. **Evidence Extraction:** Brownfield: copy exact verbatim source quotes with `file:line` citations. Greenfield: quote the story ID plus the acceptance criterion text verbatim (e.g. `US-CALC-002 AC2: "Then an error 'Cannot divide by zero' is shown"`).
4. **Actor Classification:** Assign every requirement to an actor (`anonymous`, `customer`, `admin`, `system`).
5. **Output Delivery:** Produce `02-requirements/requirements.json` and present for Gate 1 human approval.

## Strict Rules
- See [references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md](references/REQUIREMENT_RULES.md) for anti-hallucination and evidence guidelines.

## Platform code step
Before Gate 1 is presented, the platform runs the contract check in code (planned: `qe/contracts.py`, not yet built). It returns `{accepted, rejected}` and fails if any requirement has no evidence quote or, when a repository root is given (brownfield), if the quote is not found verbatim in its source file. Drop or fix every rejected requirement. It writes nothing.

# Extracting Requirements

Reverse-engineers observable functional behavior into structured, traceable requirements without hallucination.

Activate when the requirements stage runs (plugin command `qe-requirements`), or whenever deriving testable behavior from source code, API routes, or Jira stories.

# Requirements Reverse-Engineering Rules

1. **Observable Behavior Rule:** Requirements must assert externally observable behavior (HTTP response codes, return values, emitted events, DOM changes). Never assert internal private variable state.
2. **Mandatory Source Quote Rule:** Every requirement must include:
   - `source_file`: relative path to real file.
   - `line_number`: 1-based start line.
   - `quote`: verbatim code snippet copied directly from source.
3. **Precedence Rule:** Executable code strictly takes precedence over comments. If a comment says "Always returns true" but code has an `if (...) return false;` branch, extract the real code behavior.
4. **Actors Rule:** Every requirement names exactly one actor or `system`.

1: # 💰 Personal Finance MCP
2: 
3: > Deterministic personal-finance toolkit exposed over the **Model Context Protocol** — 77 calculators, a meta-advisor, and live market data, with a polished web UI. Grounded in established financial mathematics.
4: 
5: <!-- mcp-name: io.github.sarveshtalele/personal-finance -->
6: 
7: [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10+-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org)
8: [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-streamable--http-blueviolet)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
9: [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-137_passing-brightgreen)](tests/)
10: [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
11: [![Live on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/demo-Hugging%20Face-yellow?logo=huggingface&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sarveshtalele/personal-finance-mcp)
12: 
13: **Live demo:** https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space
14: **Connector URL:** `https://sarveshtalele-personal-finance-mcp.hf.space/mcp`
15: 
16: ## Demo
17: 
18: [![Watch the demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/G27KlYvo6SE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)
19: 
20: ▶️ **[Watch the 2-minute demo](https://youtu.be/G27KlYvo6SE)** — plain-language question → chained tools → a prioritized plan.
21: 
22: > **Public demo note:** the hosted Space is a shared, best-effort instance (rate-limited,
23: > may cold-start after idle). For heavy or private use, run it locally or self-host
24: > (see [docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md](docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md)).
25: 
26: ---
27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Most finance "assistants" guess at numbers. This one doesn't. It ships **77 deterministic
31: calculators** — same inputs, same answer, every time — and lets an LLM route a plain-language
32: question to the right tools. Describe your situation ("I'm 30, earn ₹1L/month, want to retire
33: at 60") and the `create_financial_plan` orchestrator chains the relevant calculators into a
34: single prioritised plan.
35: 
36: It runs three ways from one codebase:
37: 
38: - **As an MCP server** — connect it to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client.
39: - **As a website** — a Next.js UI with a live calculator, a market dashboard, and a tool catalog.
40: - **As a hosted connector** — deployed to a Hugging Face Docker Space; one URL does all three.
41: 
42: ### Highlights
43: 
44: - 🔢 **Deterministic** — pure math, no model inference for the numbers.
45: - 🤖 **Story → tools** — the model maps intent to tools; users never name them.
46: - 🇮🇳 **Theory-grounded** — TVM, debt, PPF/SSY/NSC/EPF, bonds, derivatives, MPT, and more.
47: - 🛰️ **Live market data** — mutual-fund NAVs (AMFI), FX (ECB), equity quotes (Yahoo) — no API keys.
48: - 🔒 **Hardened** — stateless, rate-limited, input-bounded APIs with security headers/CSP.
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## Tool catalog — 77 tools, 13 categories
53: 
54: | Category | Tools | Examples |
55: |----------|:----:|----------|
56: | Time Value of Money | 10 | future/present value, annuity, perpetuity, EAR, real return |
57: | Portfolio Analytics | 11 | CAPM, Sharpe, Sortino, Treynor, alpha, allocation, rebalancing |
58: | Financial Planning | 9 | net worth, ratios, emergency fund, retirement, education, insurance |
59: | Small Savings (India) | 9 | PPF, SSY, NSC, KVP, SCSS, RD, FD, EPF |
60: | Mutual Funds | 7 | SIP, SWP, lumpsum-vs-SIP, CAGR, NAV, expense-ratio impact |
61: | Debt & Loans | 6 | EMI, amortization, prepayment, consolidation, invest-vs-prepay |
62: | Fixed Income | 6 | bond price, YTM, current yield, duration, convexity, zero-coupon |
63: | Derivatives | 5 | futures fair value, option payoff, put-call parity, Black-Scholes, beta hedge |
64: | Equity Valuation | 5 | DDM, two-stage DDM, P/E, DCF, dividend yield |
65: | Live Market Data | 4 | MF search, live NAV, FX rate, stock/index quote |
66: | Cash Flow & Budgeting | 3 | household cash flow, debt-to-income, contingency fund |
67: | Risk Profiling | 1
